patch.value: Inspect cited evidence freshness and affected criteria

Present pm-evidence facts for one authorized item in an item panel and the same compact SDK, CLI and HTTP response. Source roots and allowed file identities are selected by the server. No source resolution or review judgment is reimplemented.

Editing one allowed source updates only affected displayed evidence; A viewer cannot trigger schema writes or access another project sources; Unsupported backend mutation support is clearly refused; UI and compact machine endpoint have identical meaning; source freshness never claims completion

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Overlap checked against the installed CLI public SDK declarations and current pm-evidence, pm-review and pm-web agent context/contract/permission features. Core owns item reads, history, schemas and output shaping; pm-evidence owns exact fragment resolution, freshness and criterionFacts; pm-review owns judgments; existing web views carry receipts. This feature only presents authorized pm-evidence facts. Acceptance: changing one allowed source changes only its evidence rows; viewer inspection performs no schema writes and cannot select other project sources; mutation attempts return typed remedies; UI, SDK, CLI and compact endpoint share one response. No import/export/sync, journal, status interpretation, idempotency key or mutable coordination state is introduced. Read-only observations re-read SDK state before returning; no transaction isolation is claimed (upstream #1620).

value.text: Implemented one read-only fact page through pm-evidence check(record:false), criterionFacts, producer citation schemas/replay and guarded file/json adapters. Host-injected SDK clients use noExtensions; linked project sources only, network-only UI/SW, no schema setup or mutation dispatch. Genuine PostgreSQL HTTP validation passed: viewers read identical SDK facts, methods refuse 405 unsupported, untrusted scope/query fields refuse 400, other projects and revoked users refuse 404, settings/history unchanged. Desktop/mobile browser assertions passed for selective source refresh and stale-row clearing; adjusting probe teardown to use the harness-owned pool lifecycle. Immutable public-main tracker validation: 190/190 items, zero refusals, zero citation rows (explicit corpus limitation), maximum 107 estimated tokens, 411 read-only source files, 72427 ms, source hash unchanged. No isolation guarantee: native item re-read detects concurrent changes; the final-read and authorization-to-response windows remain documented.

value.text: Re-review repair scope: invariant 1 is authorization of the actual opened source object, including final targets and aliases, before reading or emitting any bytes; lexical linked-path checks alone are insufficient. Invariant 2 is independence of current-source resolution from retention of the historical cited fragment; current file/JSON fragments must be rendered from the same verified snapshot using pm-evidence resolution. Audited shared service adapters, HTTP route, SDK client, CLI command, UI renderer, JSON/TOON serialization, non-git fixtures and packed consumers. No inline reviewer findings or non-blocking code findings are published on the PR beyond the two orchestrator blockers; quota/disabled review notices are not approval. Branch is clean and origin/main is already an ancestor (4 ahead, 0 behind), so no merge is needed. The queue forbids sub-agents; independent boundary and bypass review passes will be performed directly. Installed pm-evidence public exports have no read-only fragment resolver/current text option; upstream public declarations and issues were checked. Requested narrow sibling-export authorization while implementing descriptor-based source policy in pm-web.

value.text: Opened-object repair now checks the canonical target and the opened file descriptor before bytes are read, refuses private/external aliases and multiply linked files, and checks descriptor/path identity and revision again before publication. Adversarial real-SDK plain-tracker tests passed all 40 provider/retention/private-alias combinations plus four deterministic directory-swap boundaries, with safe direct/chained/directory aliases as positive controls. The genuine PostgreSQL viewer route, SDK and CLI JSON/TOON regression passed (1 test), including retained private-alias redaction and unchanged schema/history. Behavioral revert proof in a disposable copy: replacing only readApprovedEvidence with the previous public fileAdapter reader makes the 40-case private-alias regression fail (boundary expected); the reviewed checkout was never modified by the mutant. Whole-package file-read audit found no other viewer-controlled project-source byte reader: remaining readers consume fixed package/static files, local process/config files or public fleet manifests. Current JSON fragment regression separately fails all five exact raw-span cases (escaped pointer, large integer, nonfinite JSON exponent, escaped string, prototype-named member and root selection) because current text incorrectly uses the absent original. The needed public pm-evidence signature is resolveFragment(text, descriptor): Fragment; it exists internally but is absent from root exports. Public SDK declarations and upstream issues were checked; sibling API authorization is pending. No workaround or weakened test is used.
